preamble: All clues must have a word removed before solving. These words, along with the completed grid, will be extremely helpful in identifying the cause of a stampede 20 years ago this month and a related phrase. Across clues contain five words and down clues five more which hint at who was responsible. Unclued entries indicate nine words which must be written above.

clue.text: Blue screen — not working

definitions.meaning: first meaning: feeling low or depressed
second meaning: out of action, as a crashed computer system is

explanation.walkthrough: 'screen' is the removed word (S); with it the clue suggests a computer's blue screen of death.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective covers both low spirits and a system that has stopped functioning.

clue.text: Being ambivalent, is to pass up artist — this'll show who's boss!

indicators.note: is to X means the letters of is change into X

parts.note: an organism is a living being

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to go is to pass, as a turn passes
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: Torn between options, a painter is passed over, but a chart settles who is in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ambivalent' is the removed word (A). GO read 'up' is OG; with RA it makes OGRA, and 'is to' that means the IS of ORGANISM becomes OGRA.
explanation.definitionFit: An organogram is a chart of an organisation's hierarchy, showing who reports to whom.

clue.text: Heads to sleep on a small bench

indicators.note: in a down clue on means the first piece sits above what follows

parts.note: to nap is to sleep briefly
per means a, as in so much a head
S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: People drift off for a nap on a little seat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bench' is the removed word (B). In a down clue 'on' stacks the first piece above the rest. Napper is dated British slang for the head.
explanation.definitionFit: Napper is old British slang for the head, so nappers are heads.

clue.text: Issue the other Tesla bonnet?

parts.note: T is the symbol for the tesla, the SI unit of magnetic flux density
a bonnet is a kind of hat

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about a car part, the bonnet of the electric car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue' is the removed word (I). Tesla looks like the car maker; it is the physics unit.
explanation.definitionFit: In 'this and that', that is the other one of the pair.

clue.text: British show disapproval of retracted tabloid howler

indicators.note: something retracted is drawn back, so the word is reversed

parts.note: to boo is to jeer in disapproval

explanation.surface: The British jeer when a newspaper withdraws a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tabloid' is the removed word (T). 'retracted' turns the jeer round into OOB; the surface wants a newspaper retraction, but the definition is the blunder itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A boob is a silly blunder, the same as a howler.

clue.text: Finally some manic paparazzi snatch photo for local newspaper?

definitions.note: the question mark admits this is a definition by example

indicators.note: finally asks for the closing letter of each of the words that follow

parts.note: the last letters of some and manic
the final letters of snatch and photo, still under Finally once paparazzi is removed

explanation.surface: A local rag gets its picture when frantic photographers grab a shot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'paparazzi' is this clue's removed word; its P starts the phrase the removed words spell. 'Finally' takes the last letters of some, manic (EC) and snatch, photo (HO).
explanation.definitionFit: Echo is a common title for British regional papers, such as the Liverpool Echo.

clue.text: Runner with stamina and energy

parts.note: con is Italian and Spanish for with, as in chilli con carne
go means energy or vigour, as in full of go

explanation.surface: An athlete with endurance and drive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stamina' is the removed word (S). A runner here is a river, not an athlete.
explanation.definitionFit: Rivers are said to run, so the Congo in Africa is a runner in crossword terms.

clue.text: Get to entomb archer giving away the latest king carelessly

indicators.note: done carelessly, the remaining letters are thrown into a new order
giving away means the archer loses the letter named next

parts.note: R (rex) is king, and here it is the final letter of archer

explanation.surface: A burial instruction for a bowman who has lost his monarch's favour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entomb' is the removed word (E). 'giving away' the last R of ARCHER leaves ACHER, which 'carelessly' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: To reach a place is to arrive at it, which is what 'get to' means.

clue.text: Revolutionary referee behind circle from which competitors throw

indicators.note: behind puts the revolutionary after the circle in the answer

parts.note: a circle is the shape of the letter O
Che Guevara, the Argentine revolutionary

explanation.surface: A rebel official stands back from a ring where athletes hurl things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'referee' is the removed word (R). CHE goes 'behind' O. The definition looks like a shot-put ring, but it is the line in darts.
explanation.definitionFit: The oche is the line behind which a darts player stands to throw.

clue.text: The token man was injured capturing what sounds like an ass

indicators.note: capturing means the other letters hold the next piece inside them

parts.note: he is the pronoun for a man

indicators.note: injured letters are knocked into a different order

parts.note: taken as written
Eh? is a way of saying what?

explanation.surface: A token-gesture man got hurt catching a donkey's bray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'token' is the removed word (T). WAS 'injured' gives AWS; HE plus AWS is 'capturing' EH.
explanation.definitionFit: A donkey brays with a hee-haw, so it heehaws.

clue.text: Killer knight in Germany's rather hot

parts.note: N is the chess notation for a knight
'Rather!' is an old British exclamation meaning yes, and the German for yes is ja

explanation.surface: A murderous knight is quite warm in Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hot' is the removed word (H). 'Rather!' as an emphatic yes is dated British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Ninjas were Japanese covert agents trained as assassins.

clue.text: Any roll regularly taken from pub fixture is fine to consume

indicators.note: taken from means these letters are removed from the pub fixture

parts.note: a pool table is a standard fitting in a British pub

indicators.note: regularly picks every other letter of roll, its second and fourth

parts.note: the second and fourth letters of roll

explanation.surface: Something taken from a bar's furnishings turns out to be safe to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Any' is the removed word (A). 'regularly' takes OL from roll, and that is 'taken from' POOL TABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Potable describes water or drink that is safe to swallow.

clue.text: Drunk sons ejected from Passport to Pimlico at opening

indicators.note: drunk as in reeling, so the letters stagger into a new order
ejected from means the sons are thrown out of the words before them

parts.note: S is the genealogical abbreviation for son, so two sons are SS
taken as written

explanation.surface: Tipsy young men are thrown out of a screening of the Ealing comedy as it begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pimlico' is the removed word (P), breaking up the film title Passport to Pimlico. SS 'ejected from' PASSPORT TO leaves PAPORTTO; with AT it is 'Drunk', rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Potato trap is old slang for the mouth, the opening that potatoes go into.

clue.text: Evergreen forward always upset under realistic City manager

indicators.note: in a down clue under puts these pieces below the manager

parts.note: Pep Guardiola manages Manchester City football club
forward means cheeky, pert

indicators.note: in a down clue upset turns the word upside down, so it reads backwards

parts.note: e'er is the poetic short form of ever

explanation.surface: A veteran striker throws a tantrum beneath a pragmatic football boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'realistic' is the removed word (R). EER 'upset' is REE; PERT and REE go 'under' PEP. 'Evergreen forward' suggests an ageless footballer; the definition is the tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The pepper tree is a South American tree that keeps its leaves all year.

clue.text: Dabbler given leave returns bored by advanced sudoku

indicators.note: bored by puts a letter inside, like a drill hole
returns means the word for leave is read backwards

parts.note: to let is to leave or allow
A is the abbreviation for advanced, as in A-level

explanation.surface: An amateur granted time off comes back worn out by a hard number puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sudoku' is the removed word (S). LET 'returns' as TEL, which is 'bored by' A. A teal is a dabbling duck, one that feeds at the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Teal are ducks that dabble, tipping up to feed in shallow water.

clue.text: Country club briefly held vessel awaiting delivery

parts.note: the United Nations is a club whose members are countries

indicators.note: briefly means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: borne means carried or held

explanation.surface: A golf club's ship is kept waiting for a delivery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessel' is the removed word (V). 'briefly' cuts BORNE to BORN.
explanation.definitionFit: A baby still in the womb is unborn, awaiting its delivery at birth.

clue.text: River craft taking hours turning once you go through this

parts.note: the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

indicators.note: turning means the word for craft is reversed
taking means holding the next piece inside

parts.note: craft means skill, art

explanation.surface: A riverboat taking hours to turn round, one you pass through once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'once' is the removed word (O). ART 'taking' H makes ARHT, which 'turning' makes THRA. 'go' is the joke: to go is to urinate. The Ure is a Yorkshire river.
explanation.definitionFit: The urethra is the duct that carries urine out of the body, so when you go, it passes through it.

clue.text: Some weeks ago Pat escaped floods

parts.note: the final letter of weeks, where the run of letters starts
the first two letters of escaped, where the run ends

explanation.surface: A while back, Pat got away from the rising water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ago' is the removed word (A). Without it, 'Some' asks for a run of letters hidden across weekS PATES caped: the S of weeks, all of Pat and ES.
explanation.definitionFit: Spates are sudden river floods, as in a river in spate.

clue.text: Naff moment in street with TV presenter

parts.note: ST is the address abbreviation for street
Ant McPartlin is half of the British television double act Ant and Dec

explanation.surface: An embarrassing moment out in the street with a television host.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Naff' is the removed word (N); naff is British slang for tacky.
explanation.definitionFit: An instant is a moment, a very brief space of time.

clue.text: Thatcher's manifesto material years before substantial growth

definitions.note: manifesto is the removed word, so the definition is Thatcher's material, a roofer's thatch

indicators.note: before places the years ahead of the growth

parts.note: Y is the abbreviation for year or years
an elm is a big tree

explanation.surface: Margaret Thatcher's manifesto took years to grow into something substantial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manifesto' is the removed word (M), and without it Thatcher is a roofer, not the prime minister. Y goes 'before' ELM.
explanation.definitionFit: A yelm is a bundle of straw laid ready for thatching a roof.

clue.text: He noted tern and dove flying in Michigan park

indicators.note: in places the shuffled birds between the letters for the state

parts.note: MI is the postal abbreviation for Michigan

indicators.note: flying birds scatter, so their letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher records seabirds and doves on the wing in a Michigan park.
explanation.walkthrough: 'park' is the removed word (P). TERN and DOVE, 'flying', make ONTEVERD, which goes 'in' MI. 'He noted' looks like a birder; it is a man who wrote music.
explanation.definitionFit: Claudio Monteverdi was an Italian composer, a man who set down musical notes.

clue.text: Day for one girl, possibly Diana, to cross island

indicators.note: to cross is to lie across, so the actress's surname wraps round the letter

parts.note: Diana Dors was a British film actress, so one Diana is Dors

explanation.surface: A daytrip for a girl called Diana, perhaps, over to an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'girl' is the removed word (G). DORS is 'to cross' I.
explanation.definitionFit: Doris Day was an American singer and actress, so Doris is one example of a Day.

clue.text: Quickly impressing sultry fox dropping by to converse

parts.note: sultry weather is hot

indicators.note: dropping means the fox loses the letter that by stands for

parts.note: taken as written
X means by, as in a 3 x 4 room

indicators.note: the converse of a word is that word turned around

explanation.surface: A seductive fox calls in for a chat and speedily wins someone over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'impressing' is the removed word (I). 'by' is X as in multiplication, so the fox dropping it leaves FO; 'to converse' reads like chatting, but converse means turned round, OT.
explanation.definitionFit: Hotfoot is an adverb for hurrying, going at speed.

clue.text: Leader leaves bistro to squirrel away rent

indicators.note: the leader is the first letter, and it leaves the word

parts.note: to store something is to squirrel it away

explanation.surface: The boss walks out of a cafe to hide away the rent money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bistro' is the removed word (B). The 'Leader leaves' STORE. 'rent' is the past tense of rend, not money paid.
explanation.definitionFit: Rent is a past form of rend, to tear, and tore is the usual one.

clue.text: Undergo reaction to hurt chippy rejecting outsiders

indicators.note: rejecting the outsiders drops the first and last letters

parts.note: chippy means touchy, quick to take offence

explanation.surface: Someone goes through a painful reaction with a sulky carpenter shunning strangers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Undergo' is the removed word (U). TOUCHY 'rejecting outsiders' loses T and Y. Chippy is also British slang for a carpenter.
explanation.definitionFit: Ouch is the cry people let out when something causes them pain.

clue.text: Stunning item on radio posed from the right

indicators.note: reading from the right means the pieces are taken backwards

parts.note: re means on or concerning
to sit for a portrait is to pose, so posed is sat

explanation.surface: A dazzling radio feature was staged from the political right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'radio' is the removed word (R). RESAT read 'from the right' gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A Taser is an electric weapon that stuns its target.

clue.text: At last Spurs can transfer Eastern European

indicators.note: at last asks for the final letter of the following word

parts.note: the last letter of Spurs
can and lav are both slang for a toilet

explanation.surface: Tottenham Hotspur can finally sign a player from Eastern Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transfer' is the removed word (T). 'At last' takes S from Spurs, Tottenham Hotspur, a London football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Slavs are the peoples of Eastern Europe who speak Slavonic languages.

clue.text: Timid individual's ego picked up — a fine thing!

indicators.note: picked up as by an ear, so the word is said aloud

parts.note: a hare is a famously timid animal; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: A shy person's self-esteem gets a boost, which is a fine thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ego' is the removed word (E). HARE, 'picked up' by ear, gives the answer. 'fine' means thin here, not good.
explanation.definitionFit: A single hair is a very slender strand, the standard example of something fine.

clue.text: What's sculled in choppy ocean?

indicators.note: a choppy sea is rough and broken up, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A riddle about what gets rowed through a rough sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sculled' is the removed word (S); what is left, 'What's in choppy ocean?', is both the wordplay, OCEAN made 'choppy', and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A canoe is a light boat propelled through the water by oars or paddles.

clue.text: Indigo happy she'd periodically skipped recess

indicators.note: letters skipped at regular intervals leave every other one

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters of these words

explanation.surface: Someone cheerful in deep blue missed the break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Indigo' is the removed word (I). With letters 'periodically skipped', happy she'd leaves its even letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An apse is a semicircular recess at the end of a church.
